messages.subject: 2-armed bandit task
parts:
Dear developers and users,
I am a newbie of hbyesDM, currently  I am trying to use Hierarchical Bayesian Modeling of the 2-Armed Bandit Task to analyze my behavioral data(in my experiment, subjects were asked to choose one better choice from two shapes. (within-subject factor:stable and volatile; between-subject factor: treatment and drug) ). Now I have already fitted one model using “bandit2arm_delta” from hBayesDM package in R. Next I would like to find an identical model to analyze it again then I can further do model comparison but it is difficult for me to find another appropriate model in hBayesDM package. Could you give me some advice? Thanks so much!

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: 2-armed bandit task
parts:
Hi Nora,

I would check out the banditNarm models. Here, "N" indicates the number of different stimuli/actions that people can take. Since you are using the bandit2arm model, these other models should work too. That said, I think the input file will need to be slightly different, so you would want to check the help files for those models before trying to fit them. 

Let us know if that helps!

Best,
Nate

messages.author: 7b88d332a5071367
messages.subject: Re: 2-armed bandit task
parts:
Hi young,

Thanks for your reply. Yes, Nate is correct. In my experimental task, subjects were similarly asked to choose one from two shapes on each trial. I separated subjects into two groups(drug and PLC) so l need to do a group comparison. Based on some studies I thought bandit2arm_delta of hByesDM  match my paradigm so I used it. Now what I am confused about is that I have no idea which another model in hByesDM is proper to do a model comparison with  bandit2arm_delt. Model comparison is a necessary step for modeling. At present, I picked prl_rp of  hByesDM but I am not definitely sure whether it matches my paradigm. If you want to see more details about my task, you can see this paper(Learning the value of information in an uncertain world httphttps://www.nature.com/articles/nn1954s://www.nature.com/articles/nn1954). There is a difference between this task and mine. I did not set various reward magnitudes like this reference. In my task, if feedback is correct subjects obtain 1 score, incorrect obtain  0 score on each trial. Look forward to your suggestions. Thanks for your help again.

Best,
Nora
